  "text": "On Thursday afternoon, Marcus took the long way home to avoid a road closure. The detour led him past the community garden, where a woman was struggling to keep a gate open while steering a wheelbarrow through it. He stopped to hold the gate, and she introduced herself as Noor, one of the garden volunteers.

Noor explained that a delivery of compost had arrived earlier than expected. The bags needed to be moved under the shelter before the forecast rain. Marcus had no urgent plans, so he offered to help. Noor found him a pair of spare gloves, and together they carried bags from the pavement to the garden’s storage area.

As they worked, Marcus noticed small wooden signs beside the beds. Some marked vegetables he knew, like carrots and beans, while others named plants he had never grown. Noor told him that each volunteer looked after a bed but that everyone shared the watering. When they reached the last bag, dark clouds had gathered above the rooftops.

Marcus returned the gloves and headed for the gate. Before he left, Noor pointed to a notice listing the garden’s open hours. She said visitors were welcome, even if they only wanted to look around. Marcus photographed the notice just as the first drops of rain began to fall.

The following Sunday, he came back with his daughter, who wanted to see the sunflowers Noor had mentioned. They spent half an hour walking between the beds. On their way out, his daughter asked whether they could grow something at home. Marcus said they could start with a pot of beans."
